Password-protected or plain copies of your records
Preselected when you reopen the idle timer. Also enables one-tap Start from the widget and Quick Settings. Never changes a running session.
No preferred project. Quick Start is available only when a single project is eligible.
This preference stays on this device and is not included in backups. Archived or missing projects are not used.
The saved project is unavailable. Automatic selection is used.
Hide project names in notifications, the home-screen widget and Quick Settings. This does not encrypt the local database.
Pause, resume or stop from the notification while a session is active. Notification sounds are controlled by Android.

This file is NOT encrypted or password-protected. Anyone with the file can read and change your projects, notes, work history and included settings. Save it only in a trusted place. A password-protected copy is safer.

This copy has no password or authenticity protection. Only open files from a source you trust. The next screen checks the structure and shows what will be imported; it cannot prove who created the file.
Not encrypted or authenticated. These counts describe structurally checked data, not a trusted or signed file.
This is not a supported backup, or its contents are damaged.
Pause or stop the timer before making a copy: only confirmed, closed intervals are saved. A running interval is not included.
Password-protected: .otmbackup. Without password: .otmplain. Both can restore records; CSV cannot.
Step-by-step help, timer recovery and safe backups. Available offline.

1. Open Timer. Use “No project” or create a project with a name and color.
2. Select a project and tap Start. The timer counts elapsed time even if the screen is off.
3. Pause for a break, then Resume. Stop finishes the entry and sends it to History.
4. Add a note to an active session and save it before leaving the note editor. A daily goal is a visual target, not an alarm or an automatic stop.

Choose a project on Timer. Switching projects during a running or paused session finishes the previous entry and starts a new one; two timers cannot run together.

In Settings → Tracking and projects, choose a default. It is preselected on a fresh idle screen and used for quick Start from the widget or tile. An explicit selection in the app and the project of an active session take priority.

Automatic selection has no preferred project; system quick Start requires exactly one eligible project. Archiving a project keeps existing history but makes it unavailable for new sessions. A missing or archived default falls back safely. The default preference is local and is not transferred in a backup.

Allow notifications to use Pause, Resume and Stop without opening the app. If Android blocks them, Timer still works inside the app. Open the notification settings from Timer or Settings → Android and device.

Add the OTM widget using your launcher’s widget picker. Add the tile using Android’s Quick Settings editor. While idle, quick Start uses your default project; without one, it starts only when a single project is eligible. Otherwise the app opens so you can choose.

“Hide project names on system surfaces” protects names in these controls, but not the contents of your database or backup files.

History lists completed sessions. Search by project or note. Use Add entry to record work you did not time. Enter the local date, start time, duration and a project; the project picker has its own search and pagination.

Edit changes a completed entry. If you edit only its note or project, its original precise timing is retained. Changing its timing replaces the segmented entry with the duration you provide. An archived project remains available for an existing entry.

Delete is permanent after confirmation. Load more to reach older entries; history loads in bounded pages.

Reports show confirmed work intervals for a week, month or custom range of at most 10 years. Totals are split at period boundaries using your current time zone. A running interval becomes confirmed when paused, stopped or switched. The Timer screen can display that live interval before it appears in a report.\n\nExport the selected period as CSV using Android’s file picker. CSV is readable plaintext for spreadsheets, not a complete backup, and cannot be restored into the app. Keep sensitive exports private.

1. Pause or stop the timer first: copies save confirmed, closed intervals, not the current open interval.
2. Open Settings → Backups and restore. The primary action creates an encrypted .otmbackup. Use a long, unique password of at least 12 Unicode characters, up to 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Store the password separately: it cannot be recovered. Older copies with shorter passwords still open.
3. To make a copy without a password, use the separate action and read the warning. An .otmplain file exposes projects, notes, history and included settings to anyone who has it. It has no authenticity protection.
4. Keep a separate backup somewhere trusted and verify it with Inspect and restore. Backups are limited to 4 MiB and supported record counts.

Open a backup through Android’s file picker. Encrypted files require their exact password, including spaces. Unprotected files do not; only use a source you trust. Inspection checks the file before offering a preview. No records are changed at this stage.

Merge keeps local data and adds new records. Conflicting content with the same record ID blocks the operation. Replace permanently replaces local history and included settings after an additional confirmation. First make a separate copy of current data. A failed database transaction rolls back; a successful Replace has no Undo.

Restore is blocked while a session is running, paused or awaiting review. Hide the preview, finish or resolve the timer, then return to retry. Hide retains the preview only in process memory. Cancel restore discards it. If Android ends the process, open the file again.

The app uses a monotonic clock, not repeated database writes every second. The timer normally survives closing the screen or process recreation. A reboot or an invalid time reference can make the unconfirmed interval unknowable.\n\nIf Timer shows “Review required”, open its recovery action. Keep confirmed time only, or enter an end date and time you can verify. The app does not invent work time after a restart. History and reports include only confirmed work. After resolving the entry, you can start again.

Time is calculated from a saved clock anchor; no wake lock or exact alarm is needed to count seconds. Visible counters update only while needed, and system controls use event-driven updates. There is no network synchronization or analytics.\n\nAndroid or a manufacturer can still restrict background work or hide controls. Reopen the app if a notification or widget is stale. Do not disable battery protections unless you have a specific problem; the app does not require a blanket exemption. After a reboot, resolve an interrupted timer instead of assuming missing time was recorded. Battery savings vary by device and are not a battery-life guarantee.

Records stay on the device. The app has no Internet permission, account, ads or analytics. Android automatic backup is disabled; make your own copies. The local database is not independently encrypted by the app. Your device lock and storage protections still matter.

An encrypted .otmbackup is password-protected. A plain .otmplain or CSV is not. Android’s file picker may save into a cloud provider if you select one. Removing a partial file after an error can fail; follow the warning and delete it manually.

Stable releases signed with the same key update in place. If Android reports an incompatible signature, do not uninstall or clear data to force the update. First create and verify a backup and plan the transfer.
